structure.description: Individual spatial formula examples extracted from the Structure Examples showcase. Each map demonstrates one proven pattern from architecture and game design.
structure.name: Structure Grammar: Spatial Formulas
structure.truth: Space is authored, not found. Every room is an argument.

artifact_groups.rationale: Pedestal formula: elevated platform centering attention on a single object. The simplest spatial argument — elevation equals importance.
Corridor formula: linear space channeling movement. Direction without choice — the spatial grammar of sequence and procession.
Amphitheater formula: descending tiers focusing attention toward center stage. Light sphere as focal point — architecture as collective gaze.
The Drop formula: vertical reveal through descent. Unit circle as mathematical anchor in a space that uses height difference as dramatic device.
Frame formula: walls creating viewports that control what's visible. Architecture as editorial — inclusion and exclusion through structural framing.
Comparison formula: side-by-side placement forcing evaluation. Animated and static cubes paired — spatial design that makes difference visible.
Cathedral formula: vertical space producing awe through scale disparity. Height-to-width ratio as emotional architecture — the sublime through proportion.
Observation formula: elevated platform overlooking a scene below. The panopticon principle — spatial power through vantage point.
Lab Bench formula: specimens arranged at working height for close inspection. Four mathematical artifacts — Albers squares, Platonic solids, rainbow, cube scene — as research objects.
Zen Garden formula: open contemplative space with distributed focal points. Fourier, noise torus, probability sphere, unit circle as meditative mathematical objects.
Well formula: descent into contained vertical space. Spectrum display at the bottom — the well as spatial metaphor for focused, inward-looking analysis.
Portal Chamber formula: transitional space between worlds. Crystal ball as the focal artifact — architecture as threshold and transformation.
Ramp Walkpath formula: gradual elevation change as spatial narrative. Movement through height without stairs — continuous accessibility as design principle.
Transport Cube formula: enclosed mobile platform. Spatial formula for vertical traversal — the elevator as room that moves through architecture.
Teleporter formula: instant spatial relocation. Non-Euclidean connectivity — the spatial formula that breaks physical continuity by design.
Bridge formula: span connecting two separated volumes. Architecture as connection over void — the spatial grammar of crossing.
